blockers: Public G.I. 4 (FRONT PLAYFIELD) also feeds G.I. bulbs under the apron, which a parts supplier names in the owner thread on the violet string and which the retained 1.3 table suggests with two render lights under its apron instruction cards. No manual page, drawing or parts list draws them, and neither retained table models a bulb there, so their number and positions are unknown and the string's placements are incomplete. Resolution path: a recreation that models those bulbs, or a drawing that locates them, checked for number and sockets against a photograph of a FunHouse playfield with the apron removed, which any owner can take.

read_by.transcription: independent readers working only from gridded tiles of the committed excerpt crops, without table data
read_by.verification: the curator overlaid every page (reads, controls and the table placements mapped through each page's control fit) and measured every control on fine-grid crops: the three jet-bumper caps (the readers' reads, confirmed), the three flipper pivots as the centre of each bat's rounded end (replacing the readers' estimates, one of them 25 px off on the solenoid page, and adding the upper-left pivot two readers missed) and the outer frame's top corners from the frame lines' pixel profiles, which match the table bounds (leave-one-out at most 0.025); reads are kept as transcribed. Only reads whose point marks a part are checked: a number printed with no leader in open space or along an edge marks none, and its placements are listed as excluded with that reason. The cabinet-area reads 11, 12, 13, 14, 21, 22 and 88 are outside the playfield. The switch page prints 81 where no other 31 appears; the matrix marks 81 Not Used, so it is read literally and checks nothing. The three Steps switches and the three Steps lamps are measured on the drawing

drawing_callout_check.rule: A placement is validated when its own callout on the factory location drawing (each callout paired with at most one placement of its label, nearest first) lands within 0.07 normalized of it under two least-squares fits of that page: one on independently read controls (jet-bumper caps and flipper pivots, or another crisp mechanism feature where balloons hide a pivot), and one, measured leave-one-out, on the page's other callout reads, from which any read beyond the limit is dropped. Placements without such a read keep their table status. Placements measured on a drawing are never checked against it.

general_illumination.method: Public G.I. names, wires, pins, fuses and triacs come from the L-9 ROM's T.6 test. Public 1's socket is the spotlight, the RudyShade Light under the table's lamp-shade primitives (Case 1). For public 2 and 4 the retained 1.3 table draws a bulb at only some of the Lights its script drives (Case 2 GI_Upper, Case 4 GI_Lower), so the bulbs come from version 2.0c of the same table, which models a bulb (pBulb glass, pFiliment filament, pFBase base) under each Light its script assigns to the same public string (GI_UpperBulbs, GI_LowerBulbs). A socket is a 2.0c bulb with a driven 1.3 Light within 0.01 normalized; of the co-located 1.3 render doubles the placement is the one that shows its own bulb mesh, else the one on a BulbFil filament primitive, else the one with the smallest falloff radius. A 1.3 Light under no 2.0c bulb makes no socket. Both tables split the strings as the ROM's names do (Rudy's spotlight, rear playfield, front playfield) and as the owners traced the orange and violet strings, no retained table contradicts the split, and public 0 and 3 light only the backbox (docs/SPATIAL.md, G.I. string membership). The manuals draw no G.I. socket and give no per-string bulb count, so no quantity is asserted.
